summary:
Voices in the Void is a cinematic web experience and narrative universe that rescues NASA's forgotten space hardware from historical obscurity. We built a central platform featuring dedicated subpages for six carefully chosen robotic explorers, allowing each machine to tell its story in its own voice. The vision extends far beyond a standard informational website: the cinematic trailers we present are designed to tease a future where each prototype has its own fully interactive video game set in its real space environment. Due to time and skill constraints, we are presenting the web experience and the cinematic trailers, but the ultimate goal is to let users deeply experience how each piece of hardware functioned, what data it gathered, and the impact it left behind.

The six prototypes were selected strategically to forge a genuine emotional connection with young audiences. Voices in the Void addresses the challenge by turning complex engineering into an engaging, accessible narrative. It is important because it honors the silent pioneers of exploration. It reminds us that the legacy of these machines is not just in the scientific data they transmitted, but in the stories they inspire for the next generation.
details:
Project Details: Voices in the Void

Voices in the Void is an immersive web platform that functions as a digital constellation. The user navigates a central hub to access dedicated subpages, where carefully selected NASA robots are brought to life through compelling storytelling and interactive design. The platform benefits the audience by transforming dense, technical space history into an emotional, accessible narrative designed for school-age enthusiasts and casual learners.

The project's ultimate intended impact is to change how we view space exploration—from a list of past successes to a living legacy. While we are currently presenting the web experience and cinematic trailers due to time and technical constraints, these videos are not just informational. They are teasers for a much larger vision: fully interactive video games for each prototype, set in their real environments. The goal is to eventually let users deeply experience the hardware's mechanics, the data it gathered, and its profound impact.

To bring this to life, we used a robust technological stack. For AI and Audiovisual Production, we used Claude (Anthropic) for narrative development, creative direction, and coding the interactive elements. We generated animated shots and character voices using Google Flow, with scripts and documentation organized in Word and PDF. For 3D Modeling, we modeled the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle in Blender, and utilized NASA 3D Resources and Solar System Scope for high-resolution models (Ingenuity, Voyager, Cassini-Huygens, etc.) and celestial textures. For Web Development & Games, the platform is built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, utilizing Three.js and three-globe for interactive 3D scenes, including the destination map and minigames (like Cassini's gravity assist and Ingenuity's flight). We also experimented with Unity 6.3 LTS for a WebGL prototype. The site is hosted at missionrelics.earth via Porkbun, using FileZilla for large assets and GitHub as a code backup.

In this first demo, we chose to feature only six prototypes, but the website was designed from the ground up to be highly scalable, serving as an expandable hub meant to encompass many more missions and projects in the future.

Creativity lies in treating hardware as characters rather than mere objects. We designed the experience to be cinematic and poetic, moving away from a traditional museum format. Our team focused heavily on which prototypes to choose, carefully selecting machines that had the most significant scientific impact and the strongest potential for emotional connection. Crucially, we believe it is essential to recognize the human effort behind every machine. Behind each piece of hardware is a massive team of scientists and engineers whose skills and collective imagination create ideas with real, intergalactic impact; this project is a tribute to them as well.

Furthermore, we considered how the planned games would be designed to be highly accessible, ensuring that children and casual players can easily understand and play them. We believe that video games are powerful tools for influence and learning across all disciplines. Through interactive play, users can grasp complex concepts more easily, opening bridges that ignite imagination and curiosity. After all, who doesn't love to play while learning something new and having fun?
